en.name: Dried soba noodles
en.summary: Dried soba is buckwheat flour, usually cut with wheat, rolled and dried into straight bundles. Sealed and kept away from sun, heat and damp it runs about 2 years from purchase and about 1 year once opened — figures borrowed from dry pasta. Trust the date on the pack if it is shorter, because buckwheat oil makes soba stale before other dried noodles do.
en.pantry: The Japanese dried-noodle trade's own labelling rule is the one to follow: keep it out of direct sunlight, heat and damp. That gives about 2 years from purchase sealed, and about 1 year once the pack is opened and resealed in an airtight jar. Buckwheat carries more oil than wheat does, so a hot cupboard turns dried soba stale-smelling long before it becomes unsafe — the noodles start to taste dusty and flat, and the buckwheat aroma that is the entire point of them goes first. Buy small packs and store them away from anything strongly scented, because dried noodles take up smells readily.
en.fridge: Dried soba is not a refrigerated food and does not belong in a humid fridge. Cooked soba is a different matter: it is a wet starch food and must be cooled quickly and kept covered at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, not left standing in a colander. Rinse cooked soba in cold water, drain it thoroughly, and refrigerate it promptly if you are not eating it straight away — cold soba noodles left sitting at room temperature are the same hazard as any other cooked starch.
en.freezer: No freezer timeline is given for dried soba and it needs none — a sealed pack in a cool, dry cupboard covers a couple of years, far longer than the flavour lasts anyway. Freezing the dry bundles only introduces condensation. If you want to store soba beyond its best flavour, the answer is to buy less of it more often, not to freeze it.
spoilage: A dusty, stale or faintly bitter smell instead of a nutty buckwheat one.
Noodles that have taken up a smell from spices, soap or detergent stored nearby.
Bundles gone soft or bendy rather than snapping cleanly.
Webbing, small moths or mould in a pack that has been open in a humid kitchen.
tips: Buy small packs — soba is at its best long before its date.
Store away from spices, soap and cleaning products; dried noodles absorb smells.
Reseal or decant into an airtight jar as soon as you open the pack.
Follow the pack date when it is shorter than any general figure.

faq.q: How long does dried soba keep?
faq.a: About 2 years from purchase sealed, about 1 year once opened — or the pack date if it is shorter, which for soba it often is.

faq.q: Why does dried soba go stale faster than udon?
faq.a: Buckwheat flour carries more oil than wheat flour, and that oil turns, taking the aroma with it.

faq.q: How should cooked soba be stored?
faq.a: Rinsed, drained, covered and refrigerated at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, promptly. It is a cooked starch and should not sit out.

zh.name: 乾蕎麥麵
zh.summary: 乾蕎麥麵是以蕎麥粉（通常混合小麥粉）壓延乾燥成的直條麵束。密封並避開陽光、高溫與潮濕，從購買日起算約 2 年，開封後約 1 年——這兩個數字借自乾燥義大利麵。若包裝標示的期限更短，請以包裝為準，因為蕎麥的油脂會讓它比其他乾麵更早走味。
zh.pantry: 日本乾麵同業自己的標示規則就是最好的指引：避開陽光直射、高溫與潮濕。這樣未開封從購買日起算約 2 年，開封後改裝密封罐約 1 年。蕎麥的含油量高於小麥，所以一個悶熱的櫥櫃會讓乾蕎麥麵在「變得不安全」之前很久，就先出現陳味——麵吃起來乾澀平淡，而最先消失的正是蕎麥香，也就是吃它的全部理由。請買小包，並遠離任何氣味強烈的東西，因為乾麵非常會吸味。
zh.fridge: 乾蕎麥麵不是冷藏食品，也不該放進潮濕的冰箱。煮過的蕎麥麵就是另一回事：那是含水的澱粉食品，必須快速降溫並加蓋放 4 °C 以下，不能一直擱在濾網裡。煮好後用冷水沖、確實瀝乾，不馬上吃就盡快冷藏——放在室溫的冷蕎麥麵，和任何其他熟澱粉是同一種風險。
zh.freezer: 乾蕎麥麵沒有給冷凍期限，也不需要——密封放陰涼乾燥的櫥櫃就有兩年左右，本來就遠比它的風味撐得久。把乾麵束冷凍只會多帶來結露。如果你想在風味高峰之後還留著它，答案是少量多次地買，而不是冷凍。
spoilage: 聞起來乾澀、陳舊或微苦，而不是蕎麥的堅果香。
吸到了旁邊香料、肥皂或清潔劑的味道。
麵束變軟、可以彎折，而不是乾脆地折斷。
在潮濕廚房裡開封放久，出現絲網、小蛾或霉。
tips: 買小包——蕎麥麵的最佳風味遠早於保存期限。
遠離香料、肥皂和清潔用品；乾麵很會吸味。
一開封就封緊，或倒進密封罐。
包裝日期比通則數字短時，一律以包裝為準。

faq.a: 未開封從購買日起算約 2 年，開封後約 1 年；若包裝日期更短則以包裝為準——蕎麥麵常常更短。

faq.q: 為什麼乾蕎麥麵比烏龍麵更早走味？
faq.a: 因為蕎麥粉的含油量高於小麥粉，油脂一變質，香氣也跟著走。

faq.q: 煮好的蕎麥麵要怎麼保存？
faq.a: 沖冷水、瀝乾、加蓋，盡快放 4 °C 以下冷藏。它是熟澱粉，不能放在室溫。
